key_insight: A unified fracture model shows that lattice materials transition from geometry-controlled low-density fracture to nodal stress-concentration-driven failure at higher relative densities, with crack-tip shape and lattice fillets strongly affecting toughness.
engineering_relevance: Designers can use lattice geometry, orientation, and fillet radius to tune fracture toughness across a wide density range, including cases where quasi-brittle lattices can outperform the base material in crack resistance.
method: Homogenization-based analytical model for triangular and hexagonal lattices
Blunt-crack fracture theory extended to higher relative densities
Finite element simulations and laser-cut PMMA experiments for validation
evidence_signal: The analytical model is corroborated by finite element results and supported by PMMA fracture experiments, which also show roughly 1.6× toughness enhancement in quasi-brittle lattices and a strong dependence of failure on relative density.
watch_item: Brittle lattice fracture remains stochastic, so high-density predictions may be sensitive to local crack-path details, nodal geometry, and manufacturing variability.
paper_title: Fracture of Lattice Materials from Low to High Relative Density
